newsitem.title: INDIA: Hunt under way for survivors after Indian cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Hunt under way for survivors after Indian cyclone.

text.p: Rescuers scoured hundreds of devastated villages on India's southeastern coast on Saturday for survivors of a cyclone feared to have killed more than 1,000 people.
Search teams looked for victims still trapped and marooned after Wednesday's cyclone ripped through a ricebowl area, home to 2.5 million farmers and fishermen.
The official deathtoll had reached 790 by Saturday evening and Andhra Pradesh state officials feared it would exceed 1,000.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was go to the state and assess damage by helicopter on Sunday, a spokesman said.
Makeshift camps were sheltering 500,000 evacuees whose homes were laid waste by torrential rains, tidal waves, and winds of up to 180 kmph (110 mph), officials said.
On Saturday, vultures circled lazily over bloated cattle carcasses floating in a village canal swollen by floodwater.
The cyclone ravaged more than 800 villages.
"I am at a loss for words to describe the tragedy in which about 1,000 people may have lost their lives," Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu said.
Local leaders said they were unprepared for a cyclone, despite one in the state last month. Andhra Pradesh's flat low-lying coast is exposed to cyclones from the Bay of Bengal.
"This is the second cyclone in one month," said Arun Kumar, a Congress leader in Rajahmundry, at the heart of the devastation. "It was totally unexpected and a total disaster."
"But the main problem is availability of funds," he said. "The state is bankrupt and has to depend on release of funds from the central government."
Raymond Peter, a senior government official, said most of the damage had been done by high-velocity winds.

"We did evacuate low-lying areas but the damage has been caused by high winds," he said. "These have caused the house collapses and the falling of trees.. there is little anyone could have done about it."
Another official said the cyclone had been expected to hit the neighbouring Krishna district, where all was in readiness, but suddenly veered off course to the Godavari River delta.
Diwali, the most important festival in the Hindu calendar, falls next week. But it will be bitter this year for the people of Rawlapalam, a hamlet in the heart of East Godavari district.
East Godavari took the brunt of the cyclone. According to official figures an estimated 417 people have died there.
"On Wednesday night the wind came like a thundering aeroplane and shook the houses," said Venkat Reddy, a local high school principal. "Everybody locked themselves in," he added.
"We could hear the trees falling. Nobody dared move out."
Almost 40 or 50 villages were still marooned after torrential rain and tidal waves had surged up to five km (three miles) inland, officials said.
Police and troops struggled through swirling floodwaters up to three metres (10 feet) deep to reach other isolated hamlets.
Three helicopters dropped supplies to those stranded. Teams of government employees chopped up trees to clear blocked roads.
The Eenadu newspaper reported more than 1,000 fishermen were missing. Officials said establishing accurate figures would be difficult as whole villages had been wiped out.
"About 225,000 homes have been completely razed by the storm," a government official told Reuters.

Some 615,000 hectares (1.5 million acres) of rice crops were destroyed, said H.S. Brahma, who is heading the relief operation. An additional 312,000 hectares (770,640 acres) of bananas, coconuts and sugarcane were devastated.
Power lines were down.
Seven people were admitted to hospital with symptoms similar to cholera, the United News of India reported, but officials were confident any risk of an epidemic would be minimised.
Kerosene is being distributed to burn the rotting carcasses of over 4,000 head of cattle and almost a million poultry.

In 1977, more than 10,000 people were killed by a cyclone that drove a tidal wave up to 12 km (eight miles) inland. A cyclone killed 120 people in June this year, and 967 people died in another in 1990.
